getUIComponents.rationale: The tool `Provides a comprehensive list of all Magic UI components.` Component lists from an npm package/ecosystem documentation can include public third-party/registry-style content; the advertised text does not state the content is user-private or local, but it is public documentation-like content that may be attacker-influenced in the supply chain or community source. It has no inputs and no advertised write/send capability, so it is READ and not a SINK/SECRET/HOSTEXEC.

getComponents.rationale: The tool `Provides implementation details for marquee, terminal, hero-video-dialog, ... pointer components.` Implementation details for UI components are documentation/code-like public content and may be attacker-controllable through third-party package/registry or public documentation sources under the threat model. No inputs are declared and no write/send/execution is advertised.

getDeviceMocks.rationale: The tool `Provides implementation details for safari, iphone-15-pro, android components.` Such component implementation details are public documentation/package content and may be attacker-controllable via third-party sources. The description does not advertise private data access, outbound delivery, or host execution.

getSpecialEffects.rationale: The tool `Provides implementation details for animated-beam, border-beam, ... scratch-to-reveal components.` Public UI component implementation details can be authored or influenced by outside parties in registries/documentation; because the text does not settle provenance, UNTRUSTED is kept. No arguments or write capability are advertised.

getAnimations.rationale: The tool `Provides implementation details for blur-fade components.` This returns public implementation/documentation content, which can be attacker-influenced through third-party/public sources. It has no schema properties and no advertised state change, network sink, secret access, or host code execution.

getTextAnimations.rationale: The tool `Provides implementation details for text-animate, line-shadow-text, ... spinning-text components.` Public component implementation details are treated as attacker-controllable content under third-party/public registry/documentation assumptions where provenance is not settled. No write/send/execute behavior is advertised.

getButtons.rationale: The tool `Provides implementation details for rainbow-button, shimmer-button, ... ripple-button components.` It returns public documentation/code-like component details, which may be attacker-influenced in a package/registry ecosystem. It has no input properties and no described sink, secret source, or host execution.

getBackgrounds.rationale: The tool `Provides implementation details for warp-background, flickering-grid, ... interactive-grid-pattern components.` Returned component details are public third-party documentation/package content and may be attacker-controllable; the advertised text does not establish trusted authorship. No state-changing or outbound-delivery capability is advertised.

notes: All tools have empty input schemas, so there are no destination_args or value_args.
No advertised tool description mentions local files, user credentials, SaaS account data, arbitrary URLs, writes, messaging, or host command execution.
